mainTopic: The year an אתרוג and other tree fruit belong to for מעשר and שביעית, רבי נחמיה's view on one-crop trees, and ריש לקיש's challenge to the carob custom
overview: This amud begins by filling in missing words in the ברייתא of אבטולמוס. He held that an אתרוג follows picking for מעשר but follows formation for שביעית, and the vote in אושא made picking the rule for both. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש rule that a sixth-year אתרוג that carries into שביעית stays sixth-year fruit. רבין adds that this holds even if it grew hugely during שביעית, so eating it untithed is eating טבל. A ברייתא then sets ט״ו בשבט, by the time of formation (חנטה), as the cut-off for tree fruit. רבי נחמיה limits this to trees that produce 'like two broods' a year, while one-crop trees such as carobs follow the coming year. רבי יוחנן reports that people followed רבי נחמיה for carobs, and ריש לקיש challenges him from the משנה of בנות שוח. רבי יוחנן was silent, and רבי אבא הכהן tests three answers he could have given. The first two are rejected, but the third, that carob מעשר is דרבנן while שביעית is דאורייתא, stands. The amud ends by asking whether רבי יוחנן's silence meant he accepted the challenge or thought it unworthy of a reply.

steps.title: Fixing the missing words in the ברייתא of אבטולמוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier difficulty by saying the ברייתא is missing words. אבטולמוס said an אתרוג follows picking for מעשר but follows formation for שביעית. The sages at אושא then made picking the rule for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing, and this is what it really teaches: An אתרוג follows its picking for מעשר, and follows the formation of its fruit for שביעית. And our Sages voted in אושא: it follows its picking, both for מעשר and for שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the earlier problem (what did the vote in אושא add?) by filling in missing words in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As the ברייתא was first read, אבטולמוס and the vote in אושא seemed to say the same thing, so the vote added nothing new. Once we add 'and formation for שביעית' to אבטולמוס, there is a real difference. אבטולמוס split the two areas of law, and אושא made picking time decide both.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is missing words.' The text is incomplete and must be filled in.
Picking. The time the fruit is harvested.
The early formation of the fruit on the tree.
The seventh (Sabbatical) year of the farming cycle.
They counted votes. A formal vote of the sages.
Usha, a town in the Galilee where the sages met after the Bar Kochba revolt.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the vote in אושא as a repeat of אבטולמוס. The whole point of the fix is that אבטולמוס used formation for שביעית, and אושא changed only that part.

phrases.english: It is incomplete
and this is what it teaches:
An etrog follows its picking for tithes
and follows formation for the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: These are the missing words that were added.

phrases.english: And our Sages voted in Usha:
it follows its picking,
both for tithes and for the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised on the previous amud about the ברייתא of אבטולמוס.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אבטולמוס and אושא both said picking, so the vote added nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: אבטולמוס used picking for מעשר and formation for שביעית. אושא made picking the rule for both.
steps.whatToRemember: There were two positions: אבטולמוס split the rule (picking for מעשר, formation for שביעית), and אושא used picking for both.

steps.title: A sixth-year אתרוג that carries into the seventh year stays sixth-year fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both rule that an אתרוג that formed in the sixth year and is still on the tree when שביעית begins is always treated as sixth-year fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say: An אתרוג of the sixth year that entered שביעית is always considered sixth-year produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The אמוראים of ארץ ישראל give a ruling about an אתרוג that crosses from the sixth year into שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though it is picked in שביעית, it keeps the status of the year when it formed. This means that, for this case, they decide by formation (חנטה) for שביעית, like the first view of אבטולמוס. As a result, the rules of שביעית produce do not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated.' This introduces a ruling of the אמוראים.
'Both of them say.' The two sages agree.
'A daughter of the sixth.' Fruit belonging to the sixth year.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish
both say:
An etrog of the sixth year
that entered the Sabbatical Year
is always sixth-year produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ruling of the אמוראים on the same topic of the אתרוג and שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג that formed in the sixth year and is picked in שביעית keeps sixth-year status.

steps.title: Even if it grew hugely in the seventh year, it is still liable as טבל
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that a sixth-year אתרוג stays sixth-year fruit even if it was only olive-sized when שביעית began and grew to the size of a loaf. One who eats it without tithing is liable for eating טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A sixth-year אתרוג that entered שביעית, even if it was the size of an olive and became the size of a loaf, one is liable for it because of טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין adds detail to the ruling of רבי יוחנן and shows how far it goes and what follows from it in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if almost all of its growth happened in שביעית, the אתרוג still counts as sixth-year fruit. Since שביעית produce is exempt from tithes but sixth-year produce is not, this אתרוג must be tithed. Eating it untithed is a real sin of eating טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When רבין came' from ארץ ישראל to Bavel and reported a teaching.
A loaf of bread. Here it means very large.
Produce that has not been tithed and may not be eaten.
One is liable (for punishment) because of it.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the real result of this status: the fruit is not free like שביעית produce, but must be tithed.

phrases.english: When Ravin came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A sixth-year etrog that entered the Sabbatical Year,
even if it was olive-sized and became loaf-sized
one is liable for it because of untithed produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the ruling in Step 2, showing it applies even in an extreme case and has a practical result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when most of its growth happened in שביעית, a sixth-year אתרוג must be tithed. Eating it untithed is eating טבל.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוחנן, the year an אתרוג formed decides its שביעית status, no matter how much it grows later.

steps.title: ט״ו בשבט decides which year a tree's fruit belongs to
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that fruit which formed before ט״ו בשבט is tithed as part of the previous year. Fruit that formed after it is tithed as part of the coming year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A tree whose fruits formed before ט״ו בשבט is tithed for the previous year. If they formed after ט״ו בשבט, it is tithed for the coming year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets the cut-off date for tree fruit when it comes to tithes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For trees in general, the deciding moment is formation (חנטה), and the dividing date is ט״ו בשבט, the ראש השנה לאילנות of the משנה. It matters because tithes may not be taken from one year's fruit for another year's fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
The fifteenth of the month of שבט, the new year for trees.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A tree whose fruits formed
before the fifteenth of Shevat
is tithed for the previous year,
after the fifteenth of Shevat
is tithed for the coming year.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִילָן שֶׁחָנְטוּ פֵּירוֹתָיו קוֹדֶם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בִּשְׁבָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the special case of the אתרוג to the general rule for all trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tree fruit is assigned to a year by the time it formed, with ט״ו בשבט as the dividing line.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה limits the rule to a certain kind of tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says the ט״ו בשבט rule applies only to a tree that 'makes two broods in a year.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said: In what case are these words said? With a tree that makes two broods in a year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה narrows the ברייתא so it applies only to one type of tree. His unusual wording sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of the ברייתא is not thrown out. It is limited to trees with a certain growing pattern. The word 'broods' (בריכות) normally describes animals, which is why the גמרא questions it next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In what case were these words said?' This introduces a limitation of a ruling.
Broods, litters (as of animals or birds).

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said:
In what case are these words said?
With a tree that makes two broods in a year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the ברייתא in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ט״ו בשבט rule is said about a tree that produces in a 'two broods' pattern each year.

steps.title: Trees do not have broods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי נחמיה: how can a tree produce 'two broods'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Two broods — could that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the word 'broods,' since only living creatures have broods. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the law itself, only on the wording. A tree does not literally give birth to broods, so the phrase cannot be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Could it enter your mind?' A sign that the plain reading is impossible.

phrases.english: Two broods — could that enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי נחמיה in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'שתי בריכות' in the words of רבי נחמיה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Broods belong to animals, not trees, so the literal wording makes no sense.

steps.title: Read it as 'like two broods'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: the tree produces something like two broods, meaning two waves of fruit in a year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording so that 'two broods' is a comparison and not literal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the word 'like' (כעין) makes the phrase a description of the tree's pattern: its fruit comes in two batches, the way animals have litters. The law of רבי נחמיה stays the same; only the wording is adjusted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, say.' This introduces a corrected reading.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
like two broods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tree literally produces 'two broods,' which is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tree produces fruit in a pattern similar to two broods, meaning two batches of fruit in a year.

steps.title: Trees with one crop a year go by the coming year
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי נחמיה's view. Trees that yield once a year, such as dates, olives and carobs, are tithed by the coming year even if their fruit formed before ט״ו בשבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a tree that makes only one crop a year, like date palms, olive trees and carob trees, is tithed as part of the coming year, even if its fruit formed before ט״ו בשבט.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes רבי נחמיה's statement. It tells us what happens to trees that do NOT produce two waves of fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נחמיה, the ט״ו בשבט formation date only matters for trees with two crops a year. A tree with one crop is not judged by when its fruit formed. So even fruit that formed before ט״ו בשבט counts toward the coming year, because it is judged by when it is picked.

keyTerms.meaning: One brood: a single crop of fruit per year

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this means the fruit's formation before ט״ו בשבט is simply ignored for everyone. This is רבי נחמיה's view only. The רבנן (תנא קמא) apply the formation rule to all trees.

phrases.english: But a tree that makes one brood,
for example, date palms, olive trees and carob trees,
even though their fruits formed
before the fifteenth of Shevat,
are tithed as part of the coming year.
phrases.notes: They follow the time of picking, not the time of formation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי נחמיה's ברייתא by giving the other side of his distinction, now that 'two broods' has been explained in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי נחמיה, one-crop trees such as dates, olives and carobs are tithed by the coming year even if their fruit formed before ט״ו בשבט.

steps.title: People followed רבי נחמיה for carobs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that the common practice for carobs followed רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: People were accustomed to follow רבי נחמיה when it came to carobs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us how people actually behaved. For carobs, they followed רבי נחמיה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבי נחמיה's view into accepted practice, at least for carobs. Carobs give one crop a year, so they are tithed by the coming year, based on when they are picked.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי נחמיה's view, though it disagrees with the רבנן, became the practical custom for carobs.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The people were accustomed, with carobs, to follow Rabbi Nechemya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי נחמיה's rule from Step 8 to actual practice with carobs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, carobs are treated according to רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: Challenge from white figs that follow the formation year
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן from a משנה about בנות שוח, whose fruit takes three years to ripen. That משנה judges them by the year the fruit formed, not the year it was picked.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש objected to רבי יוחנן: For בנות שוח (white figs), their שביעית is in the second year of the cycle, because their fruit takes three years to grow!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's report using a משנה about בנות שוח, a kind of white fig.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White figs ripening in year two of the cycle get שביעית rules, because they formed during שביעית. This shows the law follows when fruit formed, not when it was picked. That seems to clash with treating carobs by picking time, as רבי נחמיה does.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him (from an earlier source)
White figs: a fig whose fruit takes three years to ripen

phrases.english: Reish Lakish objected to Rabbi Yochanan:
White figs: their Sabbatical year is the second year,
because they produce fruit over three years!
phrases.notes: Fruit that formed in שביעית ripens in the second year, yet keeps שביעית status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's report that the practice for carobs follows רבי נחמיה, who goes by the time of picking.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An authoritative משנה judges בנות שוח by the year the fruit formed. That contradicts going by the time of picking.

steps.title: Silence, and the answer רבי יוחנן could have given
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was silent. Later, רבי אבא הכהן asked why, since he could have answered that the משנה follows the רבנן while his report was about רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן was silent. רבי אבא הכהן said to רבי יוסי הכהן: Why was he silent? He should have said to him: I am telling you רבי נחמיה's view, and you answer me with the רבנן's view?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives no answer. A later Sage then supplies the answer he could have given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה of בנות שוח follows the רבנן, who judge all trees by when the fruit formed. רבי יוחנן never claimed that view was wrong. He only reported that for carobs, people follow רבי נחמיה. Quoting the רבנן against רבי נחמיה is therefore no real challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He should have said to him

steps.whatToRemember: This is the first of three answers רבי אבא הכהן suggests רבי יוחנן could have given. It does not hold: Step 12 shows that admitting the משנה follows the רבנן would only expose that the custom abandons the majority.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume this suggested answer works. The גמרא tests three possible answers for רבי יוחנן's silence (Steps 11, 13, 15). The first two are rejected (Steps 12, 14), and only the third, דרבנן versus דאורייתא, stands.

phrases.english: He was silent.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא הַכֹּהֵן לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַכֹּהֵן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba the Kohen said to Rabbi Yosei the Kohen:
Why was he silent?

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא לֵיהּ: אָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה,
phrases.english: Let him say to him: I am telling you Rabbi Nechemya,
and you tell me the Rabbis?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge from Step 10 on רבי יוחנן's behalf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different תנאים: the challenging source follows another opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בנות שוח משנה seems to prove that all fruit is judged by when it formed, which would contradict the practice for carobs.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed: that משנה follows the רבנן, while רבי יוחנן was reporting רבי נחמיה's view, so the two do not conflict. Step 12 rejects this proposal.

steps.title: He could not answer that, because it would mean leaving the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הכהן explains that רבי יוחנן could not have said 'the משנה follows the רבנן.' That would invite the reply: why leave the majority to follow a lone opinion?
steps.simpleTranslation: Because ריש לקיש would have said to him: You are leaving the רבנן and acting like רבי נחמיה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אבא הכהן's question from Step 11. רבי יוחנן could not answer 'the משנה follows the רבנן,' because that would make the custom look worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן admitted the משנה is the רבנן's view, he would be admitting that people follow a minority view against the majority. Normally הלכה follows the רבים, so that answer would weaken his own position instead of defending it.

phrases.english: Because he would have said to him:
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש would reply to רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: You leave the Rabbis (the majority)
and act like Rabbi Nechemya?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא הכהן's question about why רבי יוחנן was silent.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the suggested answer would expose a bigger weakness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן could simply say the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saying that would invite the challenge of abandoning the majority for a lone view.

steps.title: He should have said: I only reported a custom
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא הכהן suggests another answer. רבי יוחנן was only describing what people do, but ריש לקיש is talking about a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him say to him: I am telling you 'they were accustomed,' and you tell me about a prohibition?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא הכהן pushes again and proposes a different answer רבי יוחנן could have given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן never said the הלכה follows רבי נחמיה. He only reported how people behaved (נהגו). So the challenge from a משנה that sets down a rule (איסורא) seems to miss the point of his report.

keyTerms.meaning: let him say to him (why didn't he answer this way?)
they were accustomed / it is the practice

phrases.english: But let him say to him:
I am telling you 'they were accustomed,'
and you tell me about a prohibition?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first suggested answer was rejected, a new one is offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A report of custom is not a halachic ruling, so a משנה stating a prohibition does not contradict it.

steps.title: A custom cannot stand against a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes back: when something is forbidden, we do not let people keep a custom that goes against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he would have said to him: In a place of a prohibition, when they are accustomed, do we leave them be?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הכהן rejects רבי אבא הכהן's suggestion from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it 'just a custom' does not help. If the custom breaks a real prohibition, we must stop people, not leave them alone. So the custom-versus-prohibition answer fails.

phrases.english: Because he would say to him:
Where there is a prohibition,
if they are accustomed, do we leave them be?!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the proposed answer on principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reporting a custom is safe from a challenge about a prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: A custom that goes against a prohibition is not tolerated, so the answer fails.

steps.title: He should have said: carob tithes are rabbinic, but שביעית is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא הכהן offers a third answer. Carob מעשר is only דרבנן, while the משנה about בנות שוח deals with שביעית, which is דאורייתא. No rebuttal follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him say to him: When I speak to you, it is about the tithe of carobs, which is rabbinic, and you tell me about שביעית, which is from the Torah?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא הכהן suggests a third answer רבי יוחנן could have given. This time the גמרא offers no reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, fruits like carobs are not tithed, so carob מעשר is only rabbinic. A rabbinic matter can be more lenient and can follow a minority custom. שביעית is a Torah law, so the בנות שוח משנה has to be strict. Because the two cases are different, the challenge seems to fall away.
steps.confusionAlert: The בנות שוח משנה from Step 10 is about שביעית, not about מעשר. That is the whole point of this answer: the two cases have different levels of strictness.
steps.whyThisMatters: Nobody refutes this answer. That forces the גמרא to rethink why רבי יוחנן was silent at all.

phrases.english: But let him say to him:
When I spoke to you —
it was about the tithe of carobs, which is rabbinic,
and you tell me
about the Sabbatical Year, which is from the Torah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: כִּי אָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second answer was rejected, a third and stronger answer is proposed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah law (שביעית) cannot disprove a lenient practice in a rabbinic law (carob מעשר), so רבי יוחנן had a clear reply available.

steps.title: Did ריש לקיש really raise this challenge?
steps.stepSummary: Since a clear answer existed, רבי אבא הכהן wonders whether ריש לקיש actually raised such a weak challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבא הכהן said: I wonder whether ריש לקיש raised this objection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops looking for answers and takes a new direction. רבי אבא הכהן expresses surprise that ריש לקיש would raise such a challenge at all. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the earlier line is being dropped. The challenge from Step 10 has an obvious answer, so רבי אבא הכהן doubts it was a serious challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised it as an objection

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Abba the priest said:
I wonder whether he raised
Reish Lakish, this objection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא הַכֹּהֵן: תְּמֵיהַנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from 'why didn't he answer' to doubting the challenge itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש's challenge is so easy to answer that one wonders whether it was really raised.

steps.title: But he did raise it!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the story clearly says ריש לקיש raised the challenge, so how can we doubt it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether he raised it? But he did raise it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבא הכהן's wording from Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know from Step 10 that ריש לקיש did challenge רבי יוחנן. So 'I wonder whether he raised it' cannot be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: but he did challenge with it!

phrases.english: Whether he raised it?
But he did raise it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי אבא הכהן's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'I wonder whether he raised it'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story itself reports that he did raise it, so the doubt makes no sense.

steps.title: The real question: did רבי יוחנן accept the challenge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the doubt. The question is whether רבי יוחנן's silence meant he agreed, or whether he thought the challenge was not worth answering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: whether רבי יוחנן accepted it, or whether he did not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבי אבא הכהן's wording. The doubt is about what רבי יוחנן's silence meant, and it ends the discussion as an open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence can mean 'you are right, I have no answer.' It can also mean 'this is too weak to bother answering.' Because a good answer existed (Step 15), the second option is possible, and the גמרא leaves it unresolved.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's silence may not mean he was defeated. The challenge from שביעית (דאורייתא) can be answered for carob מעשר (דרבנן), so maybe he simply did not think it deserved an answer.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
whether Rabbi Yochanan accepted it,
or whether he did not accept it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבא הכהן doubted whether ריש לקיש raised the challenge.
steps.terutzMaskana: He doubted whether רבי יוחנן's silence meant acceptance or dismissal.
